newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung seeks to end row over court powers.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung seeks to end row over court powers.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa on Saturday sought to calm concerns that the territory's courts will not have jurisdiction over a China-appointed legislature when Beijing takes over on July 1.

A dispute arose this week when Sir S.Y. Chung, a close aide of Tung, said Hong Kong courts would not be allowed to rule on the legality of the so-called provisional legislature, which is to replace the territory's elected chamber on July 1.

Chung said the provisional legislature, which has been denounced by pro-democracy activists, had been approved by China's parliament and was therefore an "act of state" outside the control of Hong Kong courts.

Chung's statement reinforced fears in the pro-democracy camp that Beijing will not live up its promises to give Hong Kong broad autonomy when it becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China after the sovereignty handover.
But Tung, arriving from Beijing where he met Chinese Premier Li Peng, appeared to contradict his colleague.
"Hong Kong is a very free society. Any person can question any matters. Of course the SAR court can do that too," Tung told reporters.
Tung, who was selected by a China-appointed panel, made clear he himself had no problem with the provisonal body.
"But for me, the legality of the provisional legislature is assured," he said.

The leader of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, Martin Lee, has said he may launch legal action against the provisional legislature, which has met in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, just across the border from Hong Kong, to avoid court challenges.
Tung was accompanied to Beijing by Anson Chan, Hong Kong's top civil servant, who will keep her job when the British formally leave at midnight on June 30.

Chan, who was meeting Premier Li for the first time, told reporters afterwards that the Chinese leader had agreed on the importance of the rule of law in order to maintain Hong Kong's stability and prosperity.
